hints: Focus on what makes a carbon chiral, four different groups attached, and then look at what the central C=O can become.
The starting molecule is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{COCO}_2\text{H}$, addition of HCN to the ketone gives $\text{HOCH}_2\text{C(OH)(CN)CO}_2\text{H}$ with four different groups.
Compare the two reducing agents, $\text{NaBH}_4$ leaves the acid alone while $\text{LiAlH}_4$ reduces both the ketone and the acid, then check for identical groups.
walkthrough:
**Draw the starting material**

Think of it simply as $\text{HOCH}_2-\text{C(=O)}-\text{COOH}$. The middle carbon is a ketone, $\text{C=O}$, so it is flat and achiral for now.

Starting structure:
$$\text{HOCH}_2\text{COCO}_2\text{H}$$

**Reaction 1 with HCN**

HCN adds across C=O to make a cyanohydrin. The C=O becomes $\text{C(OH)(CN)}$.

Product 1:
$$\text{HOCH}_2\text{C(OH)(CN)CO}_2\text{H}$$
Now check the new central carbon. It is joined to $\text{OH}$, $\text{CN}$, $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ and $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$. That is four different groups, so it is a chiral centre. Reaction 1 counts.

**Reaction 2 with NaBH4**

Remember this key selectivity. $\text{NaBH}_4$ reduces aldehydes and ketones, but it is too mild to reduce carboxylic acids.

Product 2:
$$\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$$
The middle carbon is now $\text{CH(OH)}$. It is joined to $\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$, $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ and $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$. Four different groups again, so it is chiral. Reaction 2 counts.

**Reaction 3 with LiAlH4**

$\text{LiAlH}_4$ is much stronger. It reduces the ketone to an alcohol AND the carboxylic acid to a primary alcohol.

Product 3:
$$\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$$
This is glycerol. The middle carbon is joined to $\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$, and two identical $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ groups. Because two groups are the same, it is achiral. Reaction 3 does not count.

**Put it together**

1 gives a chiral centre, 2 gives a chiral centre, 3 gives an achiral symmetrical triol. So only 1 and 2 are correct.

options.A: This claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Reactions 1 and 2 do give chiral products, but 3 gives $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$ which has two identical $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ ends and so is achiral.
options.B: This claims 1 and 2 only are correct. Reaction 1 gives a cyanohydrin $\text{HOCH}_2\text{C(OH)(CN)CO}_2\text{H}$ with four different groups, and reaction 2 gives $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$ with four different groups. Both contain a chiral centre, while 3 does not.
options.C: This claims 2 and 3 only are correct. Reaction 2 is indeed correct, but reaction 3 is wrong because $\text{LiAlH}_4$ reduces the acid as well to give symmetrical glycerol, and reaction 1 is missed even though it does form a chiral cyanohydrin.
options.D: This claims 1 only is correct. Reaction 1 is correct, but it misses reaction 2. Students sometimes forget that $\text{NaBH}_4$ reduces the ketone while leaving $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ untouched, which still creates a chiral $\text{CH(OH)}$ centre.
